svg.title: The Project context screen — an overview card of six tiles and five numbered steps
svg.desc: A breadcrumb at the top carries the domain's own identity dot, the same colour that domain has in the Domains sidebar, in the Context sidebar and on every row below that names it. Under it an overview card of six tiles in two rows of three — Documents, Memory and Knowledge, then Agent connections, Session start and Setup — each with a one-line reading and a second line qualifying it; the first three carry a freshness dot, the last three none, because they are counts and measurements rather than ages. Then five numbered steps read top to bottom, each heading carrying only a numeral, a Title-case title and an ⓘ mark; a section's controls sit in a head row beneath that heading, above the rows, aligned to the rows' own left edge. Step one, Documents: the controls "Add from this computer", "Add from GitHub", "Write a document" and "Suggest a reading plan", then one open row, "The documents", whose size column carries a depth bar: a tinted bar behind each figure, anchored at the right, its length that document's share of the project's own total, stated plainly and never as an alarm. Step two, Memory: four closed rows — Agent connections, Handoffs, The brief and Journal — and this layer supersedes, so each save replaces the last. Step three, Knowledge: the control "+ Add a domain", then one row per domain this project draws on, each carrying that domain's identity dot, its pages, its freshness, a monitor whose entity, concept and summary counts each carry a depth bar against that domain's own page count, two doors out to Domains and to Chat, and its own Remove — this layer accumulates. Step four, Session start: a head row with three pickers — Window, Reading budget and Your tool's share — then a segmented meter drawing the context window to scale: your tool's share hatched at the left, The Curator's own layers in three steps of one violet hue, and a dashed room the width of the reading budget; then three closed rows, Documents at start, What an agent receives and How an agent reaches this. Step five, Setup: a head row saying when this computer was last checked, with Re-check; one to-fix line that is never folded — here, that the AGENTS.md Cursor reads carries older Curator instructions — with its own fix buttons; the "+ Add a tool" picker; then three closed folds, Tools, Repository on this computer and Computers, each ending in a grey tag naming how its contents travel between computers: set up on each computer, the project's git, and Personal Sync. A caption at the foot notes that the reading order top to bottom is the order a session start reads in.
svg.text: 391 KB in this project · 2 read first reach every session · the rest are opened by name
4 connections in the last 30 days · 3 saved before stopping
AGENTS.md in ~/code/curator has older Curator instructions, so Cursor may not
re-read on “continue” or save under its own name.
Replace them with the current instructions at the very top, then commit and push.
